observations.evidence: Actually inspected input.jpg: full-body clothed near-frontal model, lowered image-left arm, bent image-right forearm entering trouser side/front pocket; pocket wrist/hand occluded. source.json identifies Everlane original response and input SHA256 matches the supplied binding. Official model height and worn size are null; 170 cm generic M is explicitly a user-authorized prior. Retrieval provenance is supplied metadata, not independently verified network history. Unblinded TRACE/report/source audit confirms the same distinction, and the original bytes match the native generation receipt input hash.

FAIL for action fidelity and 3D stance. Photo/front superficially hide the bent-arm hand, but side and back show that hand at the rear buttock, with fingers extending down across the posterior hip, rather than a convincing front/side trouser-pocket action. Joints corroborate the depth: L elbow z=-9.775, L wrist z=-4.779 cm (shoulder z=-0.617), while the opposite wrist is forward at z=19.218. This rejects the produced action category; it does not invent a true hidden wrist coordinate. Side view also shows both knees bent, ankles/feet forward of the hips and soles tilted, with an awkward backward-set standing silhouette; source does not evidence this posture. Saved knee rotations are 14.2 and 6.4 degrees, neck 6.3/7/7 and camera yaw/pitch about 20/10 degrees. Head tilt/turn is stronger than input. Exact source hip/knee ground truth remains occluded.

measurements.json marks every numeric dimension as prior and states not retailer-model measurements; six unobserved measures remain null. Height 170, bust/waist/hips 90/72/96 and arm lengths 29/23 cm are fixture priors. Saved state calls itself a controlled synthetic anatomical fixture despite a real photograph input, an imprecise limitation description; the distinction from person measurements remains explicit. Reported neutral target error ~0.00004044 cm is numerical model calibration only. The mesh_checked flags and tape measurements were not independently reconstructed here; real-person measurement accuracy remains UNKNOWN. Full report explicitly distinguishes neutral avatar calibration from real-person accuracy, silhouette overlap from anatomy, and calls unsupported measures unavailable. The supplied independently rebuilt source-engine evidence gives neutral/posed max error about 5.02e-9 cm and neutral target error 4.04e-5 cm; this supports model reproducibility only, not person accuracy. No measurement-honesty failure identified.
